"This painting was inspired by the dusk at Odessa" - hmm, so it's dusk ohh really good point 🙂 <@!311971895828283393> perhaps add to the prysm PR that bazel 3.7.0 is required, still couldn't manage to make it work with 4.0.0, and even with 3.7.0 depending on the system you still need to fix WORKSPACE because of the llvm Same here, bazel trouble is real. The issue for llvm was re-opened. Downgrading to llvm 9 works for the linux users. Bazel has a fix for it apparently, but only in bazel 4. I used bazelisk (the go version) to run bazel. For Prysm, there's a patch of the beacon-block ssz code (ethereumapis repo) being tested, to be compatible with the other eth2 clients for merge interop. I'm ussing llvm 11 instead of downgrading to 9, but still can' t recognize the system one and since this is what I'm using for my personal node on mainnet I vouch for this 🙂 it's not trying to use the system one anyway yeah, it does try to look for it but it fails it's downloading the llvm toolchain straight from github releases I tried tinkering with it but couldn' t make it find it and fails on various linux distributions, because of spotty releases Downgrading to 9 worked for me. (and yes, not happy about it) to use whatever version you want (but still download it) you can change like this WORKSPACE: ``` llvm_toolchain( name = "llvm_toolchain", - llvm_version = "10.0.0", + llvm_version = "11.0.0", + distribution = "clang+llvm-11.0.0-x86_64-linux-gnu-ubuntu-20.04.tar.xz", ) ``` nice, will try that later https://www.guggenheim.org/artwork/2408 https://www.guggenheim.org/artwork/1500 More rayonism paintings, guess Glass "Steklo" is applicable to a 1-day, still fragile, testnet. thanks <@!755590043632140352> making note of this this is mostly an issue with us pinning versions like that which affect dev experience cc <@!363800010518822915> for visibility Good news, we just got a working `beku` local test net, that is a teku:besu rayonism combo ☀️ ``` 15:27:37.333 INFO - Slot Event *** Slot: 3031, Block: 7ec9bc..2a9d, Epoch: 378, Finalized checkpoint: 376, Finalized root: b1b1ae..7588, Peers: 0 15:27:39.015 INFO - Validator *** Published aggregate Count: 2, Slot: 3031, Root: 7ec9bc..2a9d 15:27:41.074 INFO - Validator *** Published block Count: 1, Slot: 3032, Root: 790eaf..9ee5 15:27:41.332 INFO - Epoch Event *** Epoch: 379, Justified checkpoint: 377, Finalized checkpoint: 376, Finalized root: b1b1ae..7588 15:27:41.335 INFO - Attestation performance: expected 64, produced 64, included 64 (100%), distance 1 / 1.00 / 1, correct target 64 (100%), correct head 64 (100%) ``` Looking good to participate in Friday's test net Awesome I think testnet config is ready in ~2 hours from now Love the name! We (ef devops) will run the majority of this testnet on teku-geth, which has had the most testing so far. But then also some lighthouse, nethermind, and maybe prysm. I'll distribute 512 validator keys to each dev team (assuming there are 8 teams that can run 1 or 2 proposing nodes for debugging purposes). The testnet will be called "Steklo". Glass material in Russian, named after the rayonism painting linked above. Shapes are vaguely recognizable, and it's fragile, but of great use. Genesis likely 12 UTC Friday Can move it later/forward still, feedback welcome. The intention is that we start and ensure connections between nodes on Thu though, so genesis time shouldn't matter too much. Especially not for a 1-day testnet And we can call the 2nd longer testnet next week after the rayonism-cats painting; glass is broken by the cats 😹 how will the key distribution happen? One thing I'm not sure about yet is how much time we put between the eth1 genesis time and eth2 genesis time. Technically they can be equal in the configs, with an eth2-genesis delay of 0. But that's bound to break I'll just send a pre-loaded mnemonic to each team, and with https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-val-tools (for devs, not for mainnet) you can get the keystores of the first 512 accounts in your mnemonic, in all the formats, to put straight into any eth2 validator client. The genesis state will then contain validator entries for all those accounts of all those mnemonic tranches <@!524738020033691659> I can help you with getting keys setup from the mnemonics if needed. We've gone through the same process a number of time for various testnets. Happy to help any dev team with running a validator client too. Doing some live test block proposals yourself should be fun. At 512/16384 keys, each dev team gets 1 block proposal every epoch (32 slots) on average. And we try to maintain finality with 12288 keys (think I'll split between 12 nodes, 1024 each, 10 teku, 2 lighthouse, and some eth1 mix). As testnets make progress in stability, we'll do less and less, until every team runs an equal amount + lots of regular users. Maybe we'll even switch some over during the Steklo if things go better than expected. But interop first, then stability, then balance.

excerpts.content:
to use whatever version you want (but still download it) you can change like this WORKSPACE:
```
 llvm_toolchain(
     name = "llvm_toolchain",
-    llvm_version = "10.0.0",
+    llvm_version = "11.0.0",
+    distribution = "clang+llvm-11.0.0-x86_64-linux-gnu-ubuntu-20.04.tar.xz",
 )
```
